title: Kafka consumer projecting support ticket events
name: Ticket event projector

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this consumer handles failures and offset commits? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A record arrives whose JSON cannot be deserialized into TicketEvent. What happens given the configuration?
choices: The container thread dies and the whole consumer group rebalances until the record expires from the topic
The poison record is skipped silently because ErrorHandlingDeserializer returns null and the listener ignores nulls
The null value triggers an IllegalArgumentException in the listener, which the error handler is told not to retry, so the record goes straight to the dead-letter topic
The record is retried three times at one-second intervals and then dropped

questions.prompt: TicketProjector.apply skips events whose version is not greater than the stored version. What does that give this consumer?
choices: Strict per-ticket ordering even if partitions are reassigned
Exactly-once consumption from Kafka without needing transactions on the producer
Protection against the DefaultErrorHandler publishing duplicate dead-letter messages
Safety under redelivery and out-of-order arrival: reprocessing an already applied event, or an older one arriving late, does not change the read model

questions.prompt: The factory sets concurrency to 3 and MAX_POLL_RECORDS to 100. Which statement is correct?
choices: Three listener threads each consume their own assigned partitions; events for the same ticket stay ordered only if they share a partition key
Each thread processes records from any partition, so events for the same ticket may be applied in parallel
With three threads, offsets are committed by whichever thread finishes first
Setting concurrency above the number of consumer groups has no effect
